gtocore.quest.tips.characteristics_of_wi: {Don't make wires carry more voltage and current than they're rated for!}

{Untreated} {wires} have a large {line loss} (and they shock you). The {longer} the run, the {more} power is lost by the time it reaches the far end. If the run is {too long}, the voltage may drop {too low}, and machines at the far end won't get enough power to run.

gtocore.quest.tips.q_7b11f10a.3fdf6549: {Yellow}: important information in the text. Anything you consider important, whether a word or a passage, can be marked in yellow.
gtocore.quest.tips.q_7b11f10a.70ff7e98: {Purple} and other colors: when other colors are already in use and you still want a different new color to highlight something. Purple is also often used in tech lines to emphasize magic-side content.

gtocore.quest.tips.q_7b11f10a.7883678b: When you feel there is already enough yellow in the text, you can absolutely use blue or other colors to mark other equally key text; colors are not mandatory, only a recommendation.
gtocore.quest.tips.q_7b11f10a.992afd68: When writing quest book descriptions, especially long passages, use colors to highlight key content, and try to distinguish different important content with different colors.
gtocore.quest.tips.q_7b11f10a.b3e22905: {Bright Green}/{Bright Blue}: usually used to mark numbers; which color to use depends on the surrounding colors. gtocore.quest.tips.q_7b11f10a.b9cd2d12: {Gray}: hint information in the text, usually used together with italics. {Hint: this is a hint} It is best to apply italics first; of course, there will be no difference in display at all.

gtocore.quest.tips.single_block_config.2: Every {machine/hatch} has a {gear-shaped} tab on its left side, where you can {check the block's facing, the state of its covers, and (for single-block machines) the direction of its inputs and outputs}.

gtocore.quest.tips.single_block_config.a: For small machines, since their input and output are combined, you can freely configure the direction of their output, decide whether output blocks input, and decide whether to auto-output:

gtocore.quest.tips.the_mysteries_of_rese: If you {can't} put the research data into the data access hatch, your data access hatch needs an {upgrade}. Only an {Advanced Data Access Hatch} can hold advanced research data.
Use the {Target Hatch} and {Source Hatch} to transfer {Research Data}.
{Research} and the {Assembly Line} will stay with you until the end of the game. Every {Assembly Line recipe} needs {Research}.
Some {Dimensional Focus Laser Etching} recipes require research, and the materials needed are an {Optical Data Stick} and the item being researched itself.
Put a {Data Stick} into the {Scanner/Research Station}, wait a while and you'll get a {Research Data Entity}; put it into a {Data Access Hatch} and the research is {successful}.
